new_findings.classification: Pre-existing malformed-resource bug; not an introduced art regression.
new_findings.finding: The missing-tag fill initializes only id=65535. Offset remains allocator contents, and lookup of that valid uint16 value reads the unset offset. A zero offset also prevents loop-index advancement.
new_findings.evidence: Untouched ttmLoadTtm/ttmFindTag compiled with actual utils.c. One real tag with declared count two: A5-filled allocation returns 2779096485 for request65535; zero-filled allocation reaches the lookup witness and times out after one second. Valid tag7 returns4; ordinary missing tag8 returns0.
new_findings.limitations: Synthetic declared/actual tag-count mismatch with deterministic allocator fills. This does not establish a failure in the shipped scripts, whose earlier corpus audit reports exact tag counts.
new_findings.suggested_backlog_text: Reject or safely represent missing TTM tag entries. ttm.c:171 sets sentinel id65535 without initializing its offset, and ttmFindTag at line69 does not advance after a matching zero offset. An actual-source headless probe with declared2/scanned1 tags returned allocator-pattern offset2779096485; zero-filled allocation hung until a1s timeout. Valid/missing ordinary-tag controls passed. Track only scanned tags or reject the mismatch and ensure lookup always terminates; preserve valid corpus behavior. This is malformed-resource evidence, not a shipped-scene regression.

new_findings.classification: Pre-existing output-I/O error propagation bug; not an introduced art regression.
new_findings.finding: The dump writers ignore stream write and close failures. dumpBmp can return normally after the stream fails to flush.
new_findings.evidence: Actual dumpBmp and utils.c executed against an isolated regular XPM output and a /dev/full output symlink. The regular control closed successfully. The full-device case observed actual fclose=-1/errno28 (ENOSPC), but dumpBmp still returned normally. The probe executable exited0. Other three dump close sites share the unchecked-close pattern by source inspection.
new_findings.limitations: Headless Linux failure injection against the actual dumpBmp helper, not a complete packaged CLI invocation. No actual disk-fill attempt or production output alteration.
new_findings.suggested_backlog_text: Propagate dump writer failures. dump.c ignores stream write/fclose results at169,235,321,570. A headless actual-source dumpBmp probe returned normally after /dev/full produced fclose=-1/ENOSPC; its regular-file control passed. Check stream completion and fail with the output filename, with valid-output and write/close-failure controls. Extractor helpers already check completion and provide a useful local pattern; current dump golden comparisons remain valuable independent coverage.
